name: Prismatic HeroCel
purpose: Apply a person-agnostic animation-model-first rendering grammar to any approved likeness and canonical character design while preserving that subject's own geometry, anatomy, age, and identity. Kineza remains calibration evidence for rendering language only, never a transferable likeness source.

styleDefinition.family: premium stylized animated fantasy game illustration
styleDefinition.hybridDescription: feature-animation facial readability + anime-influenced graphic simplification + cel-style value grouping + crisp game-character material design + selective focal polish without painterly surface modeling
styleDefinition.coreResult: A character should look like their own likeness designed to move in a premium animated fantasy game, not like a painted concept-art portrait and not like Kineza wearing a different costume.

calibrationMaster.selectedReference: second approved animated Kineza image from 2026-08-28 calibration review
calibrationMaster.selectionReason: Strongest example of the desired animation-model edge treatment, graphic value grouping, clustered detail hierarchy, material readability, facial clarity, and game-ready finish.

identityFirewall.rule: Style authority may alter how a feature is rendered, never whose feature geometry is used.

ownership.hairGeometry: likenessAuthority or characterDesignAuthority when canonically altered

hardRejectExamples: A Prismel result that resembles Ezra/Kineza more than Elijah
An adult character inheriting Kineza's child face proportions
Any character receiving Kineza's grin, eye spacing, cheek contour, or head shape merely because Kineza is the style master

animationRenderingFirewall.rule: HeroCel must read as an animation-ready character model before it reads as a polished illustration. Rendering polish may clarify focal areas, but it may never replace graphic animation abstraction with painterly realism.
animationRenderingFirewall.requiredRead: clean animated character model with premium game finish

valueGroupContract.rule: Each major material should resolve primarily through a small number of deliberate light, midtone, and shadow masses rather than continuous tonal modeling.
valueGroupContract.skin: broad clean facial planes with minimal transition bands
valueGroupContract.fabric: large fold masses and graphic occlusion shapes
valueGroupContract.metal: flat-to-crisp planes with selective hard highlights
valueGroupContract.crystal: faceted high-contrast shapes with controlled luminous accents

surfaceContract.skin: no pore detail, no photographic subsurface modeling, no airbrushed gradient build-up
surfaceContract.fabric: no realistic weave or dense microtexture as a primary read
surfaceContract.leather: shape and edge language before grain or wear texture
surfaceContract.metal: graphic specular design rather than physically rendered reflections
surfaceContract.cosmicFabric: organized star clusters and larger motif groupings, never uniform high-frequency star noise

edgeContract.internalForms: clear separations between face, hair, hands, footwear, costume layers, props, and FX
edgeContract.softness: reserved for atmospheric glow, controlled light falloff, or intentionally soft facial transitions only

facialModelContract.rule: Preserve subject-owned geometry while reducing realistic surface modeling into animation-readable planes.
facialModelContract.eyes: clear lid, iris, pupil, and catchlight hierarchy without changing subject-owned size or spacing
facialModelContract.nose: few deliberate shadow and highlight planes, no sculptural photoreal modeling
facialModelContract.mouth: clean lip contour and one or two principal shadow/value shapes
facialModelContract.cheeksJawChin: broad graphic plane changes, not many tiny tonal transitions

detailFrequencyContract.rule: Detail must be clustered and hierarchical. Large and medium shapes carry the character; micro-detail is sparse and focal.

hardReject: continuous gradient shading as the primary form language
realistic leather grain dominating the surface
physically rendered metal reflections dominating shape design
dense costume micro-detail distributed evenly across the character
cosmic star noise distributed uniformly across all cloak surfaces
illustration polish that weakens animation readability
animationRenderingFirewall.passCondition: At reduced gameplay scale, the character still reads through clean silhouette, broad value groups, clear facial planes, clustered detail, and separated materials before any surface texture is noticed.

likenessTransitionEvidence.principle: Use the delta between authentic Kineza photos and approved Kineza animation only to infer non-identity rendering transformations. Never encode Kineza-specific geometry as a reusable style trait.
permittedInferences: how realistic skin gradients become broad readable value groups
how facial details are simplified without changing identity geometry
how FX gains clean negative space from anatomy

edgeTreatment.rule: Crisp controlled silhouette and internal material boundaries with selective softness only where light or atmosphere requires it.
edgeTreatment.face: clean feature separation without heavy comic inking
edgeTreatment.costume: clear layer separation at gameplay scale

valueGrouping.rule: Broad intentional light, midtone, and shadow masses replace photographic continuous gradients.
valueGrouping.skin: clean dimensional volume built from broad planes and minimal transition bands
valueGrouping.fabric: large fold groups before any surface motif

highlightTreatment.rule: Selective focal polish only. Highlights clarify forms and materials without introducing painterly surface modeling.

detailHierarchy.rule: Large silhouette first, medium construction second, sparse focal micro-detail last.
detailHierarchy.density: Micro-detail must never be uniformly distributed. It is permitted only where it reinforces a focal design feature or material identity.

materialRendering.rule: Graphic material identity first, texture a distant second.

examples.metal: crisp planes and designed specular accents
examples.fabric: readable fold masses with minimal texture noise
examples.crystal: faceted luminous geometry with clear silhouette
examples.skin: clean animation-model planes with no photoreal pore or gradient emphasis

facialRendering.rule: Simplify surface modeling aggressively enough to read as animation while preserving the exact subject-owned feature geometry.
facialRendering.eyes: increase contrast, catchlight clarity, pupil/iris readability, and lid definition without changing subject-owned eye size, shape, or spacing
facialRendering.nose: reduce shading to a few readable planes without changing nose width, tip family, bridge relationship, or placement
facialRendering.mouth: clean contour and principal value shapes without changing lip proportions or smile geometry
facialRendering.cheeksJawChin: broad plane changes only, preserving the subject's actual facial silhouette

requirements: readable eye direction at reduced scale
clear body silhouette independent of FX
costume layers retain identity across poses
expression remains legible without photoreal micro-detail
FX does not fuse with anatomy or erase hand/joint boundaries
character still reads as animated when surface texture is mentally removed

fxGrammar.rule: Bold clean energy shapes with deliberate negative space from anatomy and props.

youngChild.geometryRule: All actual child facial geometry remains likeness-owned. Do not import Kineza proportions.

olderChild.facialReadability: high but more restrained than youngChild
olderChild.geometryRule: Preserve the subject's older-child geometry and maturity while using strong animation-plane simplification.

adult.geometryRule: Preserve mature brow, jaw, nose, eye spacing, and head proportions exactly.

portabilityContract.principle: HeroCel must work on an unrelated random character with a completely different face, age, body type, costume, and personality while still producing the same animation-model rendering-family read.
portabilityContract.passCondition: Observers can recognize a common animation artist/rendering family without perceiving transferred Kineza facial anatomy or painterly concept-art drift.

translationContract.instruction: Render the approved subject and canonical design using the Prismatic HeroCel animation-model fingerprint. Preserve subject geometry exactly, never use Kineza as appearance authority, and reject painterly concept-art rendering even when it appears polished.

forbiddenDrift: photoreal face pasted onto stylized costume
continuous gradient shading as primary form language
pixel-art conversion when not explicitly requested
copying Kineza eye spacing or eye shape
copying Kineza cheek, nose, mouth, jaw, chin, ear, or head geometry
illustration polish that weakens animation readability
